The Contracts project sits beside the module project: a nested project would need the outer project to exclude its files item by item, would put its build output inside the module tree, and shows awkwardly in IDEs.

provisions.heading: Compile Each Knowledge Area as a Model Project with Its Set Projects
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `code-placement-drift` for a folder under `src/Knowledge/` that is neither a `<Product>.<Area>/` model project nor a `<Product>.<Area>.<Variant>/` set project of a model the folder holds, and for a file directly in the Knowledge root. Review each host `Program.cs` for the `Add<Area>` call registering the sets the host runs, and each set for slice folders mirroring its model.
provisions.statement: Each knowledge area MUST compile as one `<Product>.<Area>/` model project with one `<Product>.<Area>.<Variant>/` set project per variant under `src/Knowledge/`, with slice folders by subject mirrored in each set and host composition through `services.Add<Area>(x => x.Add<Variant>())`.
provisions.rationale: One model project gives every module the same types and lookups for an area, and one set project per variant keeps each country or branch values apart without copying types into each set. Slice folders by subject, mirrored in each set, put the same subject in the same folder in the model and in every set. The host registers the sets it runs at startup, so a new variant touches the host and adds a set project while each module keeps pointing at the model.
provisions.example:
Claimwick travel area compiles as:

```text
src/Knowledge/Claimwick.Travel/                the model: row types, roles, keys, lookups, the registry, composition, validation
  PerDiem/  Mileage/                           one folder per subject
src/Knowledge/Claimwick.Travel.Germany/        one set per variant
  PerDiem/  Mileage/                           the same subjects
src/Knowledge/Claimwick.Travel.Netherlands/
```

Each host registers the sets it runs:

```csharp
services.AddTravel(x => x.Add<Germany>().Add<Netherlands>());
```

provisions.heading: Expose Only Contracts and the Entry Point
provisions.evidence: Is any type in a module project outside the entry type public? Look at the visibility modifiers in each module project.
provisions.statement: Every type in a module project outside its module entry type MUST be internal.
provisions.rationale: With one project per module, visibility forms the boundary: a public Contracts project and one public entry type, with all else internal. The compiler turns away direct use of another module internals, and the platform still discovers internal endpoints in each added module assembly. A project with one modules project holds the same visibility inside each module folder, with `LS2020` as the boundary.

provisions.heading: Follow Layer Direction in Every File
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1001` for a Domain type naming an outer-layer type, `LS2018` for an Application, Ports, or WebApi type naming a type outside its layer, `LS2025` for an adapter in `Infrastructure/{Port}/` naming a Domain type outside those or a WebApi type, and `LS2029` for another module's public query or query result named outside a handler, reaction, or job, and for another module's public command or command result named outside a reaction or job.
provisions.statement: A type MUST reference only the layers its own layer allows under the layer table of [Backend Architecture](../../core/backend-architecture.md).
provisions.rationale: A layer is a role played by a folder: a file takes its layer from its top folder in the module. Global usings import namespaces for every file, so the rule covers them too. The project references plus the folder checks join the layer table into one boundary. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-architecture#point-dependencies-inward` for .NET. | From | May reference | Enforced by | |---|---|---| | Kernel | the base class library only | project references | | Platform | Kernel and its libraries; never a module | project references | | A module | Kernel, Platform, and other modules' Contracts projects | project references plus visibility: only the Contracts project and `{Module}Module` are `public`, everything else `internal` | | A knowledge model | Kernel and its libraries | project references | | A knowledge set | Its model and the Kernel | project references | | `Domain/` | Kernel and the module's own `Domain/`, and the identifiers in other modules' Contracts projects | analyzer (folder) | | `Ports/` | Kernel, the module's `Domain/` types, the identifiers in other modules' Contracts projects, Platform abstractions; never `Application/`, `Infrastructure/` or `WebApi/` | analyzer (folder) | | `Application/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` | `Domain/`, its own use case folder, `Ports/`, `Application/ReadModels/`, the identifiers in other modules' Contracts projects, the facts its reactions answer, another module's public queries and query results with a declared `queries` edge, Platform abstractions; never another use case folder, never `Infrastructure/` or `WebApi/`, never another module's public command | analyzer (folder) | | `Infrastructure/` | `Domain/`, `Ports/` (to implement them), Platform, libraries | analyzer (folder) | | `WebApi/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` | its own `Application/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` (message and result), Kernel values, typed identifiers, Platform `Http/` and `Access/`; never `Ports/`, `Domain/` types, repositories, `Infrastructure/`, another module's public query, public command or result, or another use case | analyzer (folder) | | Hosts | Platform, each module's entry type, and the knowledge sets it registers | project references |
provisions.example:
Domain names Kernel types, its own `Domain` types, and identifiers from other Contracts projects. `Ports` adds the module `Domain` types it serves and Platform abstractions, with no `Application`, `Infrastructure`, or `WebApi` types.

Application names `Domain`, its own use case folder, `Ports`, `ReadModels`, identifiers from other Contracts, facts its reactions answer, and public queries with a declared `queries` edge. Infrastructure names `Domain`, the `Ports` it implements, Platform, and libraries. WebApi names its own Application message and result, Kernel values, typed identifiers, and Platform `Http` and `Access`.

Handlers, reactions, and jobs name another module public query or query result with a declared `queries` edge, and reactions and jobs name public commands with a declared `commands` edge. An adapter in `Infrastructure/{Port}/` names Kernel values, typed identifiers, and the types of the port interfaces it implements, with no WebApi type. A knowledge set points at its model and the Kernel, and a module points at the knowledge model it reads.

provisions.heading: Hold Each Layer in Its Own Folder
provisions.evidence: Does every module hold its Domain, Application, Ports, Infrastructure, and WebApi code in those folders, with one plural aggregate folder holding one folder per use case inside each layer that serves it, one folder per module-level read directly in each layer that serves it, every port in its own `Ports/{Port}/` folder, and every adapter in its `Infrastructure/{Port}/` folder? Look at the module folders.
provisions.statement: Each module MUST hold its Domain, Application, Ports, Infrastructure, and WebApi code in those folders, with one plural aggregate folder holding one folder per use case inside each layer that serves the use case, and one folder per module-level read directly in each layer that serves it.
provisions.rationale: The folders make each layer visible at a glance: a reader opening a module sees its domain, its use cases, its ports, its adapters, and its endpoints in the shape every .NET backend uses. A use case spreads over one folder per layer that serves it, inside the plural folder of its aggregate, and every port of the module lives in its own `Ports/{Port}/` folder with its adapter in `Infrastructure/{Port}/`. The code mirrors the records, so a reader moves between a record folder and its code folder by the same names, and the plural keeps the aggregate type visible to every handler instead of hiding it behind a singular namespace that fails with CS0118. Settled by [decision/0107-kernel-platform-and-one-project-per-module](decision/0107-kernel-platform-and-one-project-per-module).
provisions.example:
| Folder | Holds | Present when |
|---|---|---|
| `Domain/{Aggregates}/` | the aggregate with its act, part, fact, event, and refusal groupings | the module declares an aggregate |
| `Application/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` | the message, handler, validator, one definition class per concern, the result, the reaction or job that runs the use case | always |
| `Application/Settings/` | the module options class | the module binds a setting |
| `Ports/{Port}/` | the interface `I{Port}` with its signature types in `Models/` | the module declares a port |
| `WebApi/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` | the endpoint, its request and response models | the use case is reached over HTTP |
| `Infrastructure/Messaging/` | the module's message pipeline pieces | the module registers message pipeline pieces |
| `Infrastructure/Pipeline/` | the module's HTTP pipeline pieces serving no single use case | the module holds HTTP pipeline pieces |
| `Infrastructure/{Port}/` | the adapter implementing the module's port, with its options class, its wire types in `Models/`, and the collaborators it needs in `Parts/` | the module declares a port |

A module-level read drops the aggregate segment: `Application/{UseCase}/` and `WebApi/{UseCase}/`.

provisions.heading: Keep Application Types in Their Layer Folders
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `code-placement-drift` for a port folder holding no interface or more than one, for a port folder whose name is not its interface name without the `I`, for a type in a port folder outside `Models/` that the interface signatures do not name, for a type beside the adapter class outside `Models/` and `Parts/`, and for a `Models/` or `Parts/` type no adapter file names, and `dotnet build` reports `LS2018` for a `Ports/` file naming an `Application/`, `Infrastructure/` or `WebApi/` type.
provisions.statement: An application MUST place each use case's messages, results, handlers, validators, definitions, and triggers in the use case's folder inside `Application/`, every port of the module in its own `Ports/{Port}/` folder holding the interface `I{Port}` with its signature types in `Models/` and no files directly in `Ports/`, each port's adapter in its `Infrastructure/{Port}/` folder with the same folder name, holding the adapter class with its options class `{Adapter}Options.cs`, its wire types in `Models/`, and the collaborators it needs in `Parts/`, and cross-module contracts grouped by aggregate in its Contracts project.
provisions.rationale: One use case fills one folder per serving layer: its command, query, result, handler, validator, definitions, and triggers in `Application/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/`, with its endpoint and transport models in `WebApi/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/`. A module-level read drops the aggregate segment in each. A shape shared by two use cases appears in each, as `litespec/core/backend-architecture#give-each-use-case-its-own-models` states. Rules shared by two or more use cases of one aggregate live in `Domain/{Aggregates}/`. Each port of the module fills its own `Ports/{Port}/` folder, so `Ports/` shows the full list of what the module needs from outside: the interface `I{Port}` with the types its signatures name in `Models/`, with no files directly in `Ports/`. Each adapter fills `Infrastructure/{Port}/` under the same folder name, with the adapter class, its options class, its wire types in `Models/`, and its helpers in `Parts/`. Whether an interface counts as a port stays a reviewer judgment on the owning module. A module publishes data only through its Contracts project, grouped by aggregate, with no refusal and no interface in the published surface.

provisions.heading: Keep Business Values in the Kernel
provisions.evidence: Does the Kernel project hold only shared business values and the refusal exceptions of product rules, with no package reference and no project reference? Look at the Kernel project file and its files.
provisions.statement: The Kernel project MUST hold only the business values and the refusal exceptions every module uses, with no reference outside the base class library, grouped into `Domain/`, `Values/`, and `Auditing/` with no files at its root.
provisions.rationale: Only the values every module speaks live here: money, typed identifiers, dates, the aggregate root, the domain exception, the refusal exceptions of product rules, and closed sets every module uses. The Kernel takes no package reference and no project reference, so a type a domain model may use is separated from a type only a host touches by the project boundary itself. A technical capability in the Kernel would drag its libraries into every module. `Domain/` holds the aggregate base, the domain event marker, and the domain exceptions; `Values/` holds money and the typed id marker; `Auditing/` holds the audit vocabulary.
provisions.example:
```text
{Product}.Kernel/
  Domain/      AggregateRoot.cs  IDomainEvent.cs  DomainException.cs
  Values/      Money.cs  TypedId.cs
  Auditing/    the audit vocabulary
```

provisions.heading: Keep Closed Folder Sets at Every Level
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `code-placement-drift` for a folder outside its closed set or naming no declared record, for a file directly at the Kernel or Platform root, for a file in the wrong layer folder of its use case, for a reaction or job outside the folder of what it runs, for an `{Aggregates}/` folder naming no declared aggregate, for a use case folder naming no use case of that aggregate, for a file directly in an `{Aggregates}/` folder, for a singular `Domain/{Aggregate}/` folder, for a Domain type directly in `Domain/` or a use case directly in `Application/` or `WebApi/` that belongs to an aggregate, for an exception file outside `Exceptions/` and a domain event file outside `Events/`, for a state file beside its aggregate root, for a second store interface of one aggregate, for a file directly in `Ports/`, for a port folder with no adapter folder in `Infrastructure/`, for an adapter folder with no port folder, for a type beside the adapter class outside `Models/` and `Parts/`, for a `Models/` or `Parts/` type no adapter file names, for a port or adapter folder naming a declared module, for a repository implementation outside its aggregate's `Persistence/` folder, for a use-case model or adapter file in `Persistence/`, for any other file directly in `Persistence/` outside the module store contribution, for an interface in a Contracts project, for a fact in a Contracts project outside its `{Aggregates}/On{Fact}/` folder, for an event file in an `On{Fact}/` folder that names no declared event or another fact, for a fact in an `On{Fact}/` folder outside the aggregate of the domain event it translates, for a command in a Contracts project outside the `{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` folder of a public command, for a public use case message or result outside its `Contracts/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` path, for a test folder naming no declared record, for a type whose namespace does not match its folder path through its layer segment, for a folder under `Knowledge/` that is neither a model nor a set of a model the folder holds, and for a file directly in the Knowledge root; `folder-ungrouped` for a folder past 20 files that holds none of its allowed groupings; and `mark-folder-drift` for a marked element outside the folder its mark names.
provisions.statement: Each level of the Kernel, Platform, and module projects MUST hold only the folders the closed set table in this section allows.
provisions.rationale: A closed set of folders keeps each level predictable: a reader finds the same folders in every module, and review turns away the rest. Product-wide values sit in the Kernel, product-wide services sit in the Platform, and cross-module data sits in each Contracts project. Module folders track record homes, with one plural aggregate folder and one folder per use case inside each serving layer, plus one folder per module-level read. Reactions and jobs sit with the use case, notification, or external system they run, send, or call, and each read model sits in `Application/ReadModels`. A record at `modules/{module}/aggregates/{aggregates}/use-cases/{use-case}` maps to `Application/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` and `WebApi/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/`, with typed container folders dropped and names in PascalCase. A project with one modules project maps each module to one folder of that project instead.
provisions.example:
| Level | Allowed folders |
|:---|:---|
| Kernel project root | `Domain/`, `Values/`, `Auditing/`; no files |
| Platform project root | `Persistence/`, `Messaging/`, `Access/`, `Http/`, `CountryPacks/`, `Modules/`; no files; inside a capability past 20 files, one folder per sub-area. `CountryPacks/` keeps its loader and registry at its root and groups pack types into one folder per sub-area of its own naming |
| `Modules/` folder | one project folder per declared module, and one Contracts project folder per declared module |
| `Knowledge/` folder | one model project folder per knowledge area and one set project folder per variant of a model the folder holds; no files |
| Model or set project root | one folder per subject, mirrored in each set of the model |
| Module project root | `Domain/`, `Application/`, `Ports/`, `Infrastructure/`, `WebApi/`, and the entry type file |
| One modules project root, when the project keeps it | one folder per declared module |
| Contracts project root | one folder per aggregate with anything public, in the plural, and one folder per public module-level query; no files |
| Contracts `Contracts/{Aggregates}/` | the aggregate identifier when another module carries it, the types facts or messages of more than one aggregate carry when the aggregate owns the concept, one `On{Fact}/` folder per fact about the aggregate another module consumes, and one folder per public query or public command of that aggregate; no other files |
| Contracts `Contracts/{Aggregates}/On{Fact}/` | the fact type with the types only it carries; no other files |
| Contracts `Contracts/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` and each public module-level query folder | the message, its result, and the result parts; no other files |
| Module `Contracts/`, in the one modules project only | one folder per aggregate with anything public, in the plural, and one folder per public module-level query; no files |
| Module `Domain/` | one folder per declared aggregate, in the plural |
| Module `Domain/{Aggregates}/` | the root's main file, the repository interface as the aggregate's store interface, the root's partial files for a concern no single act owns (`{Root}.{Concern}.cs`), `{Act}/` per root action, `Parts/`, `Facts/`, `Events/`, `Exceptions/` |
| Module `Domain/{Aggregates}/{Act}/` | the partial file `{Root}.{Act}.cs`, the act's inputs, its private rules, and the steps only it calls |
| Module `Domain/{Aggregates}/Parts/` | the aggregate's entities, value objects, state types, and the stateless rules several acts share |
| Module `Domain/{Aggregates}/Facts/` | values passed in from other modules or the country pack |
| Module `Application/` | one folder per declared aggregate that has use cases, one folder per declared module-level read, `Notifications/`, `ExternalSystems/`, `ReadModels/`, `Settings/` |
| Module `Application/{Aggregates}/`, `WebApi/{Aggregates}/` | one folder per use case declared under that aggregate; no files |
| Module `Application/Settings/` | the module options class; no other files |
| Module `Ports/` | one folder per driven port of the module; no files |
| Module `Ports/{Port}/` | the interface `I{Port}` and `Models/` |
| Module `Ports/{Port}/Models/` | every type the interface's signatures name |
| Module `Infrastructure/` | `Persistence/`, `Messaging/`, `Pipeline/`, one folder per port the module implements |
| Module `Infrastructure/Messaging/` | the module's message pipeline pieces: the domain-to-module event mapping, audit writers, and the resolvers and mappers the module registers into the message pipeline; files only |
| Module `Infrastructure/Pipeline/` | the module's HTTP pipeline pieces serving no single use case: middleware, authorization conditions, authentication handlers; files only, past 20 files one folder per protocol holding that protocol's wire types beside its pieces. A protocol endpoint that serves one use case sits in that use case's `WebApi/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` folder |
| Module `Infrastructure/{Port}/` | the adapter class, its options class `{Adapter}Options.cs`, `Models/`, and `Parts/` when the adapter calls helpers; several adapters of one port sit side by side |
| Module `Infrastructure/{Port}/Models/` | the external system's wire types: requests, responses, file records |
| Module `Infrastructure/{Port}/Parts/` | the helpers the adapter calls |
| Module `Infrastructure/Persistence/` | the module store contribution, and one folder per aggregate with a repository; no other files |
| Module `Infrastructure/Persistence/{Aggregates}/` | the aggregate's repository implementation, stored documents, and mapping |
| Module `WebApi/` | the aggregate use case folders and module-level read folders of use cases reached over HTTP |
| Module `Application/Notifications/` | one per notification a reaction or job of the module sends |
| Module `Application/ExternalSystems/` | one per external system a reaction or job of the module calls |
| Module `Application/ReadModels/` | one per declared read model of the module, in the plural |
| Each use case folder and each folder under `Notifications/`, `ExternalSystems/`, `ReadModels/`, and `Settings/` | Files only |

```text
{Product}.Kernel/
  Domain/      the aggregate base, the domain event marker, the domain exceptions
  Values/      money, the typed id marker
  Auditing/    the audit vocabulary
{Product}.Platform/
  Persistence/  Messaging/  Access/  Http/  CountryPacks/  Modules/
Modules/{Product}.Spending/
  SpendingModule.cs
  Domain/
    Expenses/            Expense.cs  IExpenseRepository.cs  Submit/  Parts/  Facts/  Events/  Exceptions/
  Application/
    Expenses/
      SubmitExpense/     command, handler, validator, definitions, result
    ReadExpenseDirectory/  a module-level read with no aggregate folder
    Notifications/
      MemberRemoved/       a reaction that sends this notification
    ReadModels/
      ReimbursedExpenses/  a read model of published facts
  Ports/
    ReceiptPdf/          IReceiptPdf with its signature types in Models/
  Infrastructure/
    Persistence/Expenses/  the repository with its stored documents and mapping
    Messaging/           the domain-to-module event mapping, audit writers
    ReceiptPdf/          the adapter with its wire types in Models/ and helpers in Parts/
  WebApi/
    Expenses/
      SubmitExpense/     endpoint with request and response models
Modules/{Product}.Spending.Contracts/
  Expenses/
    ExpenseId.cs  OnExpenseReimbursed/ExpenseReimbursedModuleEvent.cs  ReadExpense/
  ReadExpenseDirectory/
```

provisions.heading: Keep Composition in Hosts
provisions.evidence: Does every host compose its process in `Program.cs` and host registration modules through `AddPlatform` and `AddModules`? Check each `Program.cs`.
provisions.statement: Compose each host in `Program.cs` and host registration modules: register transport services there and call `AddPlatform` and `AddModules`.
provisions.rationale: Domain and Application state abstractions for hosts to wire. A registration call inside either layer flips the dependency direction and drags Infrastructure into layers that stay clear of it. Each module registers its own types through its entry type, and `Program.cs` calls `AddPlatform()` and `AddModules(...)` in one visible order, so two hosts share wiring through the platform. This provision binds [Backend Architecture](../../core/backend-architecture.md) for .NET.
provisions.example:
The platform call, the modules call, and the endpoint map, in order:

```text
AddPlatform(...)     persistence, messaging, access, auditing, HTTP, country packs
AddModules(...)      one entry type per module that runs in this host
MapEndpoints(...)    the endpoints the platform discovered
```

`Program.cs` shows the call order. The platform owns endpoint discovery, Problem Details, refusal mapping, and JSON; the host owns transport security, authentication, authorization, and OpenAPI.

provisions.heading: Keep Each Identifier with Its Owner
provisions.evidence: Does every business identifier live in the Contracts or Domain folder of the module owning its aggregate, and does every Kernel identifier have a decision record naming the Contracts cycle it breaks? Look at each identifier beside its aggregate record and the decision records.
provisions.statement: A business identifier MUST live in the project of the module that owns its aggregate, in `Contracts/{Aggregates}/` when another module carries it and in `Domain/{Aggregates}/` otherwise, except in the Kernel with a decision record naming the Contracts cycle it breaks.
provisions.rationale: An identifier points at its aggregate, so it lives where the aggregate lives: in the owner Contracts project when another module carries it, beside the `On{Fact}` folders and the public queries and commands of that aggregate, and in `Domain/{Aggregates}/` when no other module carries it. A copy placed by convenience drifts into three copies across consumer, Kernel, and owner. The Kernel holds an identifier only to break a Contracts cycle, and only with a decision record naming that cycle. The marker generic code uses for converters lives in the Kernel.
provisions.example: `ExpenseId` belongs to `aggregate/spending.expense`. The reporting module carries it, so it lives in `Claimwick.Spending.Contracts/Expenses/ExpenseId.cs`. An identifier no other module carries stays in `Claimwick.Spending/Domain/Expenses/`.

provisions.heading: Keep Host Endpoints in Hosts
provisions.evidence: Does every host endpoint without a handler live in its host project and carry its mark? Check the host endpoints beside the use case folders.
provisions.statement: Each host endpoint without a handler MUST live in its host project.
provisions.rationale: Protocol endpoints, static assets, and development-only tooling belong to no use case folder, so the host keeps them. Each still carries its mark, and the placement check accepts a host endpoint in the host.

provisions.heading: Keep Implementation Types Internal
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2001` for an implementation type that is not `internal sealed`.
provisions.artifact: command-handler, query-handler, validator, reaction, repository, endpoint
provisions.statement: A handler, validator, definition, persistence implementation, or endpoint implementation MUST be declared `internal sealed`.
provisions.rationale: A public type is visible to every assembly, so a public handler invites calls outside its design. Messages, results, and ports turn public only inside the Contracts project, while handlers, validators, and implementations stay `internal sealed`. Assembly scanning reads internal types through the module entry type, so scanning gives no reason to widen visibility. This provision binds [Backend Architecture](../../core/backend-architecture.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Keep Technical Capabilities in the Platform
provisions.evidence: Does any Platform file name a module, its aggregates, or its use cases, or does the Platform project reference a module project? Look at the Platform sources and its project references.
provisions.statement: The Platform project MUST hold only technical capabilities that name no module, referencing only the Kernel, its libraries, and the base class library.
provisions.rationale: Persistence setup, messaging, authorization, HTTP conventions, country pack loading, and module composition are built once and stay generic. A module plugs in by contributing data, never by copying platform code. A business word in the Platform names a module the Platform never knows, and a module reference fails the build because the Platform project references no module project. Inside a capability past 20 files, one folder per sub-area groups it further, with each pack file beside the facts it reads.
provisions.example:
```text
{Product}.Platform/
  Persistence/    store setup, serializer, Money and typed id converters, discriminator registry
  Messaging/      mediators, outbox, in-process dispatch, recurring jobs
  Access/         sessions, authorization guards, composable policies
                  (Permission, RecentSignIn, Self, System)
  Http/           endpoint discovery, problem details, refusal mapping, JSON
  CountryPacks/   pack loader and dated lookups
  Modules/        IModule contract and AddModules(...)
```

provisions.heading: Keep Use Case Folders Isolated
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2019` for a use case folder naming a type in another use case folder.
provisions.artifact: use-case, command-handler, query-handler, validator, endpoint, reaction
provisions.statement: The folders of one use case MUST reference no type in the folders of another use case, except the command a reaction or job sends for the use case its record names in `onRefusal`.
provisions.rationale: The folders of one use case hold one behavior, so a link between two use case folders joins behaviors that change for different reasons. A reaction or job that runs a use case sits in that use case `Application` folder and uses the message from inside, and no handler sends a command: another module public query is the one message a handler sends, with a declared `queries` edge. A shape shared by two use cases appears in each, as `litespec/core/backend-architecture#give-each-use-case-its-own-models` states. Behavior shared more widely lives in the module or product folder that holds every consumer, as `litespec/core/backend-architecture#place-a-type-at-the-lowest-folder-that-holds-its-consumers` states. The rule covers files and global usings alike. Kernel values stay referenced directly: money, typed identifiers, dates, and closed sets the Kernel owns come from any layer the layer table allows, and WebApi models carry them on the wire. The shared `Application` folders `Notifications`, `ExternalSystems`, `ReadModels`, and `Settings` belong to no use case: a use case folder names those types freely, and the check reports no link either way.

provisions.heading: Mirror Modules, Aggregates, and Use Cases in One Namespace Tree
provisions.evidence: Does every type in the Kernel, Platform, and module projects carry the namespace its folder path implies? Compare the namespaces with the folders.
provisions.statement: Every type in the Kernel, Platform, and module projects MUST live in the namespace tree that starts with the product name and follows the folders below the project root.
provisions.rationale: When the namespace matches the folder path, `Claimwick.Spending.Application.Expenses.SubmitExpense` states the product, module, layer, aggregate, and use case without a map. A reader moves from a Domain aggregate to its handler, its repository, and its endpoint by name alone, following folders under [Naming and Code Style](../../workspace/naming.md). Each project takes its own name as its root namespace, so every namespace still starts with the product name. The aggregate folder is plural, so the namespace never hides the aggregate type the way `...Application.Expense.SubmitExpense` hides `Expense`. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-architecture#organize-code-by-module-aggregate-and-use-case` for .NET.
provisions.example:
The Expense aggregate of Claimwick's Spending module fills one branch:

```text
Modules/Claimwick.Spending/Domain/Expenses/Expense.cs
Modules/Claimwick.Spending/Application/Expenses/SubmitExpense/SubmitExpenseCommandHandler.cs
```

The handler in the tree above has namespace `Claimwick.Spending.Application.Expenses.SubmitExpense`.

provisions.heading: Name No Business Identifier in the Platform
provisions.evidence: Does any Platform file name a module identifier? Look at the Platform sources beside the module Contracts projects.
provisions.statement: The Platform MUST name no business identifier.
provisions.rationale: The Platform carries the tenant and the actor across modules: the execution identity tenant and the principal subject. A business identifier in the Platform ties every module to a copy owned elsewhere, so each module converts at its own edge. The workspace module turns the tenant string into `WorkspaceId` and back, while the Platform tracks the tenant.
provisions.example: The workspace module converts the tenant string into `WorkspaceId` at its edge and back when it answers; the Platform names only the tenant.

provisions.heading: Place Each Read Model in Its Application Read Models Folder
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `code-placement-drift` for a class carrying a read-model mark outside its read-model folder, and for a folder under `ReadModels/` that names no declared read model.
provisions.statement: Each read model MUST live in a folder named for the read model in the plural inside its `Application/ReadModels/` folder, holding the read-model document, one projection per source event named `{ReadModel}On{Fact}Projection`, the reader interface `I{ReadModel}ReadModel` and its implementation, each carrying the read model's mark.
provisions.rationale: A read model gathers answers from module events and integration events and serves the reads of its module. Beside a use case it reads as a reaction, so it sits with the other read models instead: one folder per model shows every event that fills it and the one reader its use cases call. The mark on each class points to the record that names its sources. A projection that writes past its own read model is an unrecorded reaction.
provisions.example:
```text
Modules/Claimwick.Reporting/Application/ReadModels/ReimbursedExpenses/
  ReimbursedExpense.cs                                        the read-model document, keyed by ExpenseId
  ReimbursedExpenseOnExpenseReimbursedProjection.cs           one projection per source event
  ReimbursedExpenseOnExpensePersonalDataErasedProjection.cs
  IReimbursedExpenseReadModel.cs                              what Reporting use cases read
  ReimbursedExpenseReadModel.cs                               its store implementation
```

provisions.heading: Plug Modules into the Platform Through Contributions
provisions.evidence: Does any module hold serializer, store, guard, converter, or endpoint-discovery code the platform provides? Look at the module projects beside the platform registries.
provisions.statement: A module MUST plug into a platform capability by contributing data to the platform registry instead of copying platform code.
provisions.rationale: Shared code built once stays consistent: the platform owns the serializer, the guard check, the converters, and endpoint discovery. Each module adds its stored types, closed-set discriminators, policies, and routes to those registries. A copy of platform code inside a module drifts at the next platform change, while an addition composes.
provisions.example: The spending module adds its stored types and closed-set discriminators, and the platform builds the one serializer from every module addition.

provisions.heading: Publish Only Data from Each Contracts Project
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `code-placement-drift` for an interface in a Contracts project, for a fact in a Contracts project outside its `{Aggregates}/On{Fact}/` folder, for an event file in an `On{Fact}/` folder that names no declared event or another fact, for a fact in an `On{Fact}/` folder outside the aggregate of the domain event it translates, for a command in a Contracts project outside the `{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` folder of a public command, for a public use case message or result outside its `Contracts/{Aggregates}/{UseCase}/` path, for a module event or integration event record with no `On{Fact}/` folder, and for a fact type naming no declared module or integration event.
provisions.statement: Each Contracts project MUST publish only data grouped by aggregate, with no interface anywhere in the project.
provisions.rationale: Data crosses the boundary; a call shape couples every consumer to provider code. The root holds one folder per aggregate with anything public, in the plural, and one folder per public module-level query, with no files. Each `Contracts/{Aggregates}/` folder holds the identifier another module carries, the types shared across facts or messages of that aggregate, one `On{Fact}/` folder per fact another module consumes, and one folder per public query or command with its message and result at the provider `Application` path. Each fact sits in its own `On{Fact}/` folder in the aggregate of the domain event it translates, beside the public query and command folders of that aggregate, with the namespace `{Product}.{Module}.Contracts.{Aggregates}.On{Fact}`. A module-level public query sits in its own folder directly in `Contracts`. Names stay business names: `ReadBusinessQuery` with `BusinessResult`, with no transport shapes, routes, or HTTP verbs.
provisions.example:
```text
Modules/Claimwick.Spending.Contracts/
  Expenses/
    ExpenseId.cs
    OnExpenseReimbursed/
      ExpenseReimbursedModuleEvent.cs
    ReadExpense/
      ReadExpenseQuery.cs
      ReadExpenseResult.cs
    CloseExpenses/
      CloseExpensesCommand.cs
      CloseExpensesResult.cs
  ReadExpenseDirectory/
    ReadExpenseDirectoryQuery.cs
    ReadExpenseDirectoryResult.cs
```

provisions.heading: Reach Another Module Only Through Contracts
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2020` for a module reference naming another module type outside its Contracts.
provisions.statement: A module MUST reach another module only through types its Contracts project publishes.
provisions.rationale: The Contracts project is the public surface of a module, grouped by aggregate with identifiers, shared concept types, one `On{Fact}` folder per consumed fact, and one folder per public query or command. Each layer names only what it needs from another Contracts: identifiers across `Domain`, `Ports`, `Application`, and `WebApi`; facts in `Application` reactions; public queries and results in handlers, reactions, and jobs with a declared `queries` edge; public commands and results in reactions and jobs with a declared `commands` edge. With one project per module, project references plus visibility form the boundary: only the Contracts project and the entry type are public, so other internals stay out of reach. A project with one modules project draws the same line through `LS2020`. A module publishes no refusal and no interface: it answers upstream facts through public commands from its reactions and jobs, asks public queries for current values, and reshapes kept data through its own read models.

provisions.heading: Reference Knowledge Models from Modules and Sets from Hosts
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `knowledge-reference-invalid` for a module project referencing a knowledge set project, for a knowledge set project referencing anything but its model and the Kernel, and for a knowledge model project referencing a module.
provisions.artifact: knowledge-model, knowledge-set, command-handler, query-handler, reaction, job
provisions.statement: Project references MUST run from modules to knowledge models, from knowledge sets to their model and the Kernel only, and from hosts to the sets they register.
provisions.rationale: A module that points at a set ties itself to one country or branch, so modules point at the model and leave each set to the hosts that register it. A set that points past its model and the Kernel pulls operational code into per-variant values. Host registration is composition, so hosts point at the sets they run.
provisions.example: Claimwick spending points at `Claimwick.Travel`, with country projects left to the hosts. `Claimwick.Travel.Germany` points at `Claimwick.Travel` and `Claimwick.Kernel`. The API host points at both country sets to register them.

provisions.heading: Register Each Module Through Its Entry Point
provisions.evidence: Does every module expose one public entry type implementing `IModule`, and does every host add its modules through `AddModules`? Look at each module project and each `Program.cs`.
provisions.statement: Each module MUST expose one public entry type implementing `IModule` that registers everything the module holds.
provisions.rationale: The entry type is the module's only public surface beside its Contracts project: it registers the module's adapters, contributes its stored types, discriminators, policies, and routes, and gives hosts and scanners the assembly reference. Each host adds the modules that run in it through `AddModules`, so two hosts share wiring through the platform instead of through a folder beside the modules that reaches into module internals. Settled by [decision/0107-kernel-platform-and-one-project-per-module](decision/0107-kernel-platform-and-one-project-per-module).
provisions.example: `SpendingModule` implements `IModule`, and each host program calls `AddPlatform()` and then `AddModules(...)` with the modules that run in that host.

provisions.heading: Separate the Kernel, the Platform, and the Modules
provisions.evidence: Does the solution hold only the Kernel, the Platform, one project per module, the knowledge models with their sets, and their hosts, with the reference direction the dependency rules state? Check the solution file and the project references.
provisions.statement: Use a `{Product}.Kernel` project for the business values every module speaks, a `{Product}.Platform` project for the technical capabilities, one `{Product}.{Module}` project per module grouped under `Modules/`, one `{Product}.{Area}` knowledge model project per knowledge area with one `{Product}.{Area}.{Variant}` set project per variant grouped under `Knowledge/`, and WebApi and optional Worker hosts grouped under `Hosts/`, at every size.
provisions.rationale: Each module project then holds one full business capability: domain, use cases, ports, adapters, and endpoints in the module layer folders. The compiler draws the lines: the Kernel points at the base class library, the Platform skips module projects, and each module exposes its Contracts project and its entry type. Each knowledge model exposes its lookups to reading modules, with sets pointed at only by registering hosts. A project that groups every module into one modules project draws the Contracts line through `LS2020` instead. Settled by [decision/0107-kernel-platform-and-one-project-per-module](decision/0107-kernel-platform-and-one-project-per-module). The names shorten earlier patterns to what each project holds; [Lineage](../../learn/lineage.md#kernel-platform-and-port) states the sources and the names set aside.
provisions.example:
```text
apps/api/src/{Product}.Kernel/
apps/api/src/{Product}.Platform/
apps/api/src/Modules/{Product}.{Module}/              one project per module
apps/api/src/Modules/{Product}.{Module}.Contracts/    its sibling Contracts project
apps/api/src/Knowledge/{Product}.{Area}/              one model project per knowledge area
apps/api/src/Knowledge/{Product}.{Area}.{Variant}/    one set project per variant
apps/api/src/Hosts/{Product}.WebApi/
apps/api/src/Hosts/{Product}.Worker/     only when background work needs its own process
```

provisions.heading: Bind Every Keyed Setting in One Options Class
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `setting-unimplemented` (level S) for a keyed setting no options class marks, and `setting-key-drift` (level S) for a marked options class whose `SectionName` constant and property do not spell the setting's `configurationPath`.
provisions.statement: An options class that binds a setting with a `configurationPath` MUST carry an `implements` mark naming the setting, with a `SectionName` constant and property that spell the setting's `configurationPath`.
provisions.rationale: The options class turns configuration into a typed value the code reads. The mark names the promise the class holds, and the section name plus property spell the record path. Comparing the two finds a renamed section or a typo before the product starts on a default. This provision binds `litespec/core/use-cases#bind-every-keyed-setting-in-one-marked-element` for .NET.
provisions.example: Claimwick's `SpendingOptions` class declares `SectionName = "Spending"`, an `ApprovalReminderDelay` property, and `/// <implements>setting/spending.approval-reminder-delay</implements>`.

provisions.heading: Construct Aggregate Parts Only Inside the Root
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1014` for a file outside an aggregate's `Domain/` folder that constructs a type from that folder other than the root's input records and typed identifiers.
provisions.statement: A file outside an aggregate's `Domain/` folder MUST NOT construct a type from that folder other than the root's input records, typed identifiers, and the types the interfaces its class implements name in their member signatures (a repository building the query result its Domain interface returns, an adapter building the result its port returns).
provisions.rationale: The root factories and methods form the single entry point to the aggregate. A caller that constructs an entity or value object of the aggregate builds a part the root did not validate, and a caller that builds a part to pass it in takes over behavior the root owns. Callers pass plain inputs instead, and the root builds its own parts behind that boundary. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-domain#reach-an-aggregate-only-through-its-root` for .NET.
provisions.example: In the Claimwick product, the submit-expense handler constructs no expense line and no allocation. It passes the identifiers, the line inputs, and the submitted time to `Expense.Submit`, and the root builds its lines and its allocation inside the factory.

provisions.heading: Define the Shared Domain Contracts Once
provisions.evidence: Is every shared Domain contract declared once, with `DomainException` and `AggregateRoot<TId>` in their declared shapes? Check the shared contracts; `dotnet build` reports `LS5013` for a base that declares a non-virtual `Code`.
provisions.statement: Declare the shared Domain contracts once in the shared kernel Domain folder and reuse them across every module.
provisions.rationale: Every module raises events, throws domain exceptions, and identifies aggregates. A shared contract declared twice becomes two contracts that drift. Declaring `IDomainEvent`, `DomainException`, `IStronglyTypedId`, `Entity<TId>`, `IAggregateRoot`, and `AggregateRoot<TId>` once in the shared kernel Domain folder gives every module the same mechanics. `DomainException` takes the message in its constructor and declares `Code` abstract, so each refusal code lands as an override in the partial exception. Generic handling constrains its parameters with `IAggregateRoot`. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Implement Domain Services as Stateless Classes
provisions.evidence: Does every domain service stay stateless, take only Domain values, and avoid provider calls? Check each domain service.
provisions.statement: A domain service MUST be a stateless sealed class holding only a calculation that spans aggregates with no owning aggregate, accepting and returning Domain values.
provisions.rationale: A calculation with no natural aggregate owner still belongs somewhere explicit. The stateless service holds that calculation apart from aggregates, with no persistence, messaging, logging, clock, authorization, or provider call. A calculation one aggregate owns stays in that aggregate root instead. The service carries a mark naming its rule, and the builder links it to the rule it computes. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-domain#use-stateless-domain-services-for-ownerless-rules` for .NET.
provisions.example: An order pricing service takes the lines and returns the total, and the order root calls it inside `Order.ConfirmPrice`. Application passes the lines and hands the returned `Money` to `Order.ConfirmPrice` as an input. The service itself holds no repository, clock, logger, or provider client, and returns no order line.

provisions.heading: Keep Clock Reads and Random Values Out of Domain
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1009` for a clock, randomness, or identifier read in Domain.
provisions.statement: Domain code MUST NOT read a clock, a random source, or a new `Guid`, so every such value arrives as an argument.
provisions.rationale: Each of `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeProvider`, `Random`, `RandomNumberGenerator`, `Guid.NewGuid`, and `Guid.CreateVersion7` returns a different value on every call. A Domain method that reads one runs differently on each run and resists fixed-value tests. Receiving each value as an argument keeps every Domain call a pure function of its inputs, and the Application layer obtains each value through the port it owns. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-domain#pass-nondeterministic-values-into-domain` for .NET.

provisions.heading: Keep Domain Free of Outer-Layer Concerns
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1001` for Domain code naming an outer-layer type.
provisions.statement: Domain code MUST reference only the .NET base class library and product-owned Domain types.
provisions.rationale: Business behavior stays testable while it points at the base library and product-owned types. A persistence or web reference inside Domain ties each rule to a framework release, so a provider change reaches behavior it has nothing to do with. Infrastructure registers persisted discriminators and mappings, which leaves Domain free of serialization attributes. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.
provisions.example: In Claimwick, the expense aggregate compiles against money, typed identifiers, and its own parts, with the Marten serializer and its converters registered in Infrastructure.

provisions.heading: Keep Double and Float Out of Exact Quantities
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1008` for a `double` or `float` type in Domain.
provisions.statement: Domain code MUST NOT declare a `double` or `float` for a monetary amount, a rate applied to one, or a quantity compared for exact equality.
provisions.rationale: `double` and `float` render most decimal fractions approximately, so two amounts that read as equal compare as different. The shared `Money` object holds a `decimal`, and a rate applied to a `Money` amount is a `decimal` too. The analyzer reports the Domain declaration that breaks this form. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-domain#keep-binary-floating-point-out-of-exact-quantities` for .NET.

provisions.heading: Keep Repository Interfaces in Domain
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1010` for a repository interface exposing a query surface.
provisions.statement: A repository interface MUST expose only aggregate and Domain types for exactly one aggregate root, without `IQueryable`, a session, or a generic CRUD surface.
provisions.rationale: One repository per aggregate keeps the write boundary aligned with the consistency boundary: the interface loads and stages complete aggregates of its own type, and nothing else. `GetByIdAsync` throws `{Aggregate}NotFoundException` for a load that has to succeed, which frees handlers from repeating null checks, while a nullable `FindBy...Async` stays reserved for lookups where absence is normal. `IQueryable`, sessions, and generic CRUD surfaces would leak query shaping and provider behavior into Domain, so the interface exposes none of them. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Mark Each State-Changing Root Method with Its Use Case
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS5003` for a root method carrying other than one use-case mark, and `LS5002` for a mark on a reading or private method.
provisions.statement: A root method that changes state MUST carry exactly one `<implements>` mark naming its use case.
provisions.rationale: The `<implements>` mark is the XML documentation tag tying a method to the use case act it performs. The builder and the analyzer read the same link from it. A reading or private method performs no act and carries no use-case mark. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-domain#give-each-use-case-its-own-act` for .NET.

provisions.heading: Model Child Entities as Sealed Classes
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1015` for a public setter, constructor, or mutable public collection on a non-root type of an aggregate.
provisions.statement: A child entity MUST be a sealed class deriving from the project-owned `Entity<TId>`, with no public setter, mutating method, or constructor.
provisions.rationale: The project-owned `Entity<TId>` base gives the child typed identity and identity equality, so the child declares its own data and behavior. The root creates, finds, and changes its children through business methods, and a child exposes no mutable state outside the root. Construction and mutation stay internal or private, so the root alone reaches them. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Model Every Aggregate Lifecycle with State Records
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1003` for an aggregate with no `State` property, `LS1004` for a state case left unsealed, and `LS1013` for a switch that leaves a sealed state case to its discard arm.
provisions.statement: An aggregate MUST expose its lifecycle only through one `State` property backed by an abstract `{Aggregate}State` record with sealed per-state records.
provisions.rationale: An enum, a status string, a boolean flag, a parallel nullable field, or a computed state carries no state-specific data such as a publication time. State records hold each state's data where it belongs, and aggregate methods own the transitions between them. A one-state aggregate still defines its hierarchy, so later states have a home. The sealed set matches the aggregate's declared `states`, which is the link the builder follows. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Model Every Closed Set of Domain Values Without Enums
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1002` for an enum declared in Domain, `LS1013` for a switch that leaves a sealed case to its discard arm, and `LS2041` for a closed-set `Code` compared to a string literal or a refusal exception returning a raw string literal.
provisions.statement: Domain code MUST model every closed set as an abstract record base with sealed cases exposing one stable `Code`, converting labels through `FromCode`.
provisions.rationale: An enum is a named integer, so it carries no case data and admits undefined values through a cast. When a case later gains data, the enum grows parallel fields. A record hierarchy carries each case's data in its own sealed record instead. A boundary turns a label into a case through `FromCode` instead of `ToString`, which turns an unrecognized label into a validation failure rather than a silent default. Tests cover the discard path for a case added later. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Offer a Non-Throwing Parse on Validated Value Types
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1017` for a Domain struct whose constructor throws and which declares no non-throwing parse.
provisions.statement: A typed identifier or value type whose constructor throws on invalid input MUST offer a static `TryParse` that returns false instead of throwing.
provisions.rationale: A serializer and an API boundary meet invalid input as a normal case: a malformed identifier in a route, an empty value in a stored payload. When the single way in is a throwing constructor, the boundary answers a server fault for a caller mistake, and a serializer that calls no constructor rebuilds the value empty without saying so. A `TryParse` lets the boundary turn the input away with a 400 and lets a converter fail loudly on a value it reads.
provisions.example: In the Claimwick product, `ExpenseId` throws on an empty `Guid` and offers `ExpenseId.TryParse(string? text, out ExpenseId id)`. The route binding calls `TryParse` and answers 400 for `/expenses/not-an-id`; the JSON converter calls it and fails the read for a stored empty value.

provisions.heading: Raise Immutable Domain Facts
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1007` for a domain event that is not an immutable record.
provisions.statement: A domain event MUST be a public immutable record named `{Aggregate}{PastFact}DomainEvent` implementing `IDomainEvent`, carrying business data only and one mark naming its domain-event record.
provisions.rationale: The `{Aggregate}{PastFact}DomainEvent` name tells a reader which aggregate raised the fact without opening the file. The event carries business data: the typed identifiers and the values its reactions need. It carries no aggregate, session, service, mutable collection, or exception, because a mutable payload lets a reaction observe state that changed after the fact. Envelope identity, such as message and causation identity, lives on the published integration event that carries the fact outside the process. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.
provisions.example: In Claimwick, `ExpenseApprovedDomainEvent` carries the expense identifier, the approver, the amount, and the decided time. Only the expense root raises it, through `RaiseDomainEvent` on the shared base.

provisions.heading: Reference Other Aggregates by Typed Identifier
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1016` for a property of one aggregate whose type is another aggregate's root or entity.
provisions.statement: An aggregate MUST reference another aggregate only through a property typed as its typed identifier, never through a property typed as its root or entity.
provisions.rationale: An object reference between aggregates loads one aggregate's data through another, which joins their consistency boundaries and their storage. A property typed as the other aggregate's typed identifier keeps each aggregate loadable on its own. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-domain#reference-other-aggregates-by-id` for .NET.
provisions.example: In the Claimwick product, an expense holds the submitting employee as `EmployeeId`, not as an `Employee` object. Application loads the employee through its own repository when a command needs both sides.

provisions.heading: Reject Business Violations with Domain Exceptions
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1005` for a throw outside a `DomainException` subclass and `LS1006` for a domain exception that is misnamed or open.
provisions.statement: A rejected business rule MUST throw a `DomainException` subclass named `{DomainType}{Reason}Exception`, carrying the refusal `code` and one mark naming its rule.
provisions.rationale: One exception type per rule puts the stable code and the message in the type. The call site passes domain values, and two rules share a type by accident no more. A shared rule exception with caller-supplied codes lets any caller invent a code and lets unrelated rules merge silently. Each exception's code equals the refusal `code` on the result record it answers. The root factory and methods check an invariant rule, and the use-case validator or the root method checks a precondition rule. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Split a Large Root into One File per Action
provisions.evidence: Does any root file hold more than one business action or run past 500 lines without following this layout? Look at each root file beside its actions.
provisions.statement: Declare a root whose file passes 500 lines as a partial class with one folder per business action named `{Act}/`, holding the partial file `{Root}.{Act}.cs` with the action's inputs and its private rules.
provisions.rationale: A root grows with every business action it owns, and one file holding every action reads as one long listing. Splitting the root into one folder per action keeps each action readable on its own while the root stays the single entry point to its aggregate. The name is the use case act, so `Domain/Entries/PostInvoice/` mirrors `Application/Entries/PostInvoiceEntry/`, and the action rules stay private to the root.

provisions.heading: Throw Only Refusal Codes the Module Owns
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `refusal-module-foreign` (level S) for a refusal code carried from another module's code, `refusal-code-duplicate` (level S) for a refusal code two exception types carry, and `code-placement-drift` or `record-placement-invalid` for a refusal and its exception declared under different homes.
provisions.statement: Each refusal code a module declares MUST be carried by at most one exception type, in the module that declares it, under the aggregate whose set declares the refusal.
provisions.rationale: A refusal code tells the caller which module refused and why. An exception in one module that carries another module's code blames the wrong owner, and two exception types carrying one code leave the caller unable to tell which rule failed. One carrying type per code in the declaring module keeps the blame and the rule behind each code fixed. Each aggregate declares the refusals its rules raise once in its own set, with the module set keeping the refusals no aggregate raises. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Use Strongly Typed Version 7 Identifiers
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS1012` for an `Id` struct outside the strongly typed form, or a raw `Guid` as an aggregate identity.
provisions.statement: An aggregate identity MUST be a `readonly record struct` wrapping one version 7 `Guid`, declaring no implicit conversion, primitive alias, or public parameterless creation path.
provisions.rationale: A bare `Guid` parameter accepts any identifier, including an empty one and one meant for another aggregate. The typed struct turns away `Guid.Empty` and the struct default in every factory, and a misplaced identifier fails at the boundary. New values arrive from the caller: a factory takes its identifier as an argument, and a method that needs several takes a generator. Domain reads no clock and calls no static source of time or randomness, which keeps business behavior deterministic and testable. This provision binds [Backend Domain](../../core/backend-domain.md) for .NET.

provisions.heading: Keep Implementation Style Consistent
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS3004` for a concrete class with no derived type that is not sealed.
provisions.statement: Production C# MUST use file-scoped namespaces, braces on every body, explicit access modifiers, and sealed concrete classes.
provisions.rationale: File-scoped namespaces, braces on every body, explicit access modifiers, and sealed concrete classes change diff readability rather than behavior. One shared setting removes the debate from every review and keeps generated and hand-written code consistent.

provisions.heading: Match C# Files and Primary Types
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS3003` for a C# file whose name differs from its primary type.
provisions.statement: A C# file MUST contain one primary top-level type and take that type's exact name.
provisions.rationale: A file named for its type lets a reader and a tool find the type by the path. Two top-level types in one file break that lookup and merge their histories in review. Only a small private or file-scoped nested type stays with its owner.

provisions.heading: Name Every Event Type by Its Kind
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2031` for an event type whose name does not end in the suffix of its kind.
provisions.statement: An event type MUST end in the suffix of its kind: `DomainEvent` for a domain event, `ModuleEvent` for a module event, and `IntegrationEvent` for an integration event.
provisions.rationale: A codebase holds all three kinds at once: the domain event an aggregate raises for its own module, the module event other modules consume, and the integration event leaving the product. A bare `Event` suffix, or no suffix, does not say which contract the type carries: whether the fact stays inside its module, is versioned for other modules, or has external consumers. The kind suffix puts that answer in the name, beside the `Command`, `Query`, `Result`, and `Id` suffixes the Role Suffixes table assigns.
provisions.example: In the Claimwick product, the expense aggregate raises `ExpenseApprovedDomainEvent` from `Domain/Expenses/Events/`, and the spending Contracts project publishes `ExpenseReimbursedModuleEvent` from `Contracts/Expenses/OnExpenseReimbursed/` for the reporting module. A reaction keeps the fact without the suffix: `SubmitPayoutOnExpenseApprovedHandler` answers the approval.

provisions.heading: Name Every Folder and Type for Its Reason
provisions.evidence: `litespec model review` reports `name-reason-missing` (level R) for a folder or type named for the absence of a reason outside the declared shared kernel.
provisions.statement: No folder is named `Shared`, `Common`, `Util`, `Utils`, `Helpers`, or `Misc`, and no type carries one of those names or ends in `Helper`, `Manager`, `Util`, or `Utils`, outside the declared shared kernel.
provisions.rationale: A folder named `Shared` or a type ending in `Manager` states no reason in its name, and each such name collects unrelated code. The shared kernel project is the one declared exception, named in one place, so the exception stays visible instead of spreading.
provisions.example: The declared shared kernel project passes; `Billing/Helpers/` and `OrderManager` outside it are reported.

provisions.heading: Put the Cancellation Token Last
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS3002` for a cancellation token that is misplaced or misnamed.
provisions.statement: In the dotnet stack, a method that takes a `CancellationToken` MUST place it last, or second to last before a `params` array, and name it `cancellationToken`.
provisions.rationale: A token in a fixed trailing position lets every caller pass cancellation without reading the signature, and one name lets every reader tell the token from the data beside it. A token in the middle of a signature is passed in the wrong position, and a renamed token hides what it is at the call site.
provisions.example: `SubmitExpenseCommandHandler.HandleAsync` takes `SubmitExpenseCommand` and then `CancellationToken cancellationToken`, so a caller passes the data first and cancellation last.

provisions.heading: Run LiteSpec Analyzers in the Business Projects and Hosts
provisions.evidence: Does every Kernel, Platform, module, and host project file reference `LiteSpec.Analyzers` at the manifest pin with `PrivateAssets="all"`? Look at each business and host project file.
provisions.statement: Reference `LiteSpec.Analyzers` at the manifest pin, with `PrivateAssets="all"`, from the Kernel, Platform, and module projects and each host project.
provisions.rationale: The analyzers report a breach of a .NET provision in the editor and the build, at the line breaking it, with a link to the provision. Without them, a breach surfaces only in review, if at all. The analyzer package is a development dependency: it adds nothing to the built assemblies, so Domain stays package-free at run time. `LS2016` reports a pipeline-owned collaborator in a handler constructor. Its default list covers the LiteBus unit of work, idempotency store, and outbox, and a project adds its uniqueness claim service. Settled by `decision/0103-dotnet-stack-binding`, which keeps the analyzer run in the business projects and hosts.
provisions.example:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="LiteSpec.Analyzers" PrivateAssets="all" />
</ItemGroup>
```

An unreleased build is consumed the same way, through a local feed. Pack the analyzers from the LiteSpec checkout, so the package carries the analyzer, rule library, and mark reader assemblies in its analyzer folder:

```sh
dotnet pack apps/analyzers/src/LiteSpec.Analyzers
```

Then point a local source at the packages folder, with source mapping for `LiteSpec.*`:

```xml
<packageSources>
  <add key="litespec-local" value="../LiteSpec/artifacts/packages" />
</packageSources>
<packageSourceMapping>
  <packageSource key="litespec-local">
    <package pattern="LiteSpec.*" />
  </packageSourceMapping>
</packageSourceMapping>
```

A project reference to the analyzer project does not carry its dependency assemblies with it, so the analyzers fail to load. The local feed is the way.

provisions.heading: Compare Typed Identifiers by Their Underlying Values in Queries
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2032` for a query passing a list of typed identifiers as a database parameter. It reports `LS2037` for a query reading the document's own identity value inside a queryable expression.
provisions.statement: A query MUST compare typed identifiers by their underlying values instead of passing a list of typed identifiers as a query parameter.
provisions.rationale: The database driver binds a list parameter by the element type it knows. A list of typed identifiers reaches the driver as a list of an unknown structured type, and the comparison then fails or matches nothing at the database. Comparing the underlying values keeps the parameter a list of values the driver binds. Each identifier still travels as its typed form in code and crosses into its underlying value at the query.
provisions.example:
In the library product, the list-loans query takes a list of reader identifiers and compares `reader_id` against the underlying values:

```csharp
var ids = query.ReaderIds.Select(id => id.Value).ToList();
```

The query passes `ids` as its parameter, so the database compares values it binds.

provisions.heading: Keep Pipeline-Owned Collaborators Out of Handlers
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2016` for a command or query handler whose constructor takes a pipeline-owned type.
provisions.statement: A command or query handler MUST NOT take a pipeline-owned collaborator, such as `IUnitOfWork`, `IIdempotencyStore`, or `ITransactionalOutbox`, through its constructor.
provisions.rationale: The pipeline owns the unit of work, the idempotency store, the outbox, and the uniqueness claim service. A handler that takes one of them commits or reserves work outside the post-handler that owns the commit. The analyzer default list names the LiteBus types, and a project adds its own claim service to the `litespec.LS2016.pipeline_owned_types` key. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-persistence#keep-uniqueness-out-of-handlers` for .NET.
provisions.example: The submit-expense handler takes its Domain repository and no unit of work, so the commit stays in the one post-handler. A handler constructor that adds `IUnitOfWork` is reported at the parameter.

provisions.heading: Load Documents Keyed by Typed Identifiers One at a Time
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2033` for a batch document load keyed by typed identifiers.
provisions.statement: A repository MUST load documents keyed by a typed identifier one at a time instead of batching them in one load call.
provisions.rationale: A batch load call keys its lookup by the identifier form the store understands. A batch of typed identifiers reaches the store in a form its key comparison misses, so the call returns nothing or the wrong documents. Loading each document by its typed identifier through the single-document load keeps every lookup on the path the typed-identifier mapping defines.

provisions.heading: Stage Aggregate Writes Through Repositories
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS2004` for a command handler writing through a document session or database context.
provisions.statement: A command handler MUST reach persistence only through a Domain repository, never through `IDocumentSession`.
provisions.rationale: Infrastructure implements each Domain repository with the scoped session, so the handler stages work without naming a provider type. A repository that exposed the session, a generic query, or a save operation would hand the handler the provider surface the layer exists to hide. This provision binds `litespec/core/backend-persistence#stage-aggregate-writes-through-domain-repositories` for .NET.
provisions.example: The submit-expense handler takes its Domain repository and no document session, so the commit stays in the one post-handler. A handler constructor adding the session is reported at the parameter.

provisions.heading: Store Each Aggregate Root as Its Own Document
provisions.evidence: Is any aggregate stored through a parallel document type instead of as its own document? Look at the stored document types beside the aggregates.
provisions.statement: Marten MUST store each aggregate root as its own document, with no parallel document type for an aggregate.
provisions.rationale: A parallel document type duplicates the aggregate shape in Infrastructure, forcing mapping code between the two and splitting reads between two models of one thing. Storing the root keeps one shape from the handler to the disk. Infrastructure owns the JSON contract that makes it work: the store serializer handles non-public members and constructors, one registered discriminator per closed-set case, and converters for values such as `Money` and typed identifiers, while Domain carries no serialization attribute. Query handlers query the aggregate type through `IQuerySession`. This provision covers the stored aggregate; a query-shaped read document serves queries and is no parallel aggregate document. This provision binds [Backend Persistence](../../core/backend-persistence.md) for .NET. Settled by [decision/0105-store-each-aggregate-root-as-its-own-document](decision/0105-store-each-aggregate-root-as-its-own-document).

provisions.heading: Declare Marked Events and Exceptions as Partial Types
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS5006` for a marked domain event or rule exception that is not `partial`, in every project that references the analyzer package.
provisions.statement: A project that references the analyzer package MUST declare every marked domain event and rule exception as a `partial` type.
provisions.rationale: The source generator adds the runtime value as a second part of the type. A type that is not `partial` takes no second part. The generator writes a value only where no member of that name is declared in source, so a hand-written value is compared with the record rather than duplicated. A code fix adds `partial` and deletes a hand-written value equaling the record.
provisions.example: The declaration `public sealed partial record ExpenseSubmittedDomainEvent(...)` takes its generated `Classification`, while the same record without `partial` is reported.

provisions.heading: Generate Runtime Values from the Records
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `runtime-value-drift` (level S) for a hand-written value that differs from its record, and `dotnet build` reports `LS5005` for the same value.
provisions.statement: A domain event `Classification` and a domain exception `Code` MUST equal the values their records state.
provisions.rationale: The record states each identifier and refusal code once. A second hand-written copy in code is a second source that drifts. With the analyzer package installed, its source generator writes the value into the `partial` type from the mark and the record. The event `Classification` is the event identifier, and the exception `Code` is the `code` of the refusal result its rule names. Without the analyzer package, the value stays hand-written, and the check compares it with the record.

provisions.heading: Generate the Registry, Permissions, and Roles from the Records
provisions.evidence: `dotnet build` reports `LS5009` for two records generating one constant name, `LS5011` for a message two marked handlers serve with different use cases, and `LS5012` for a role allowing a permission no record declares.
provisions.statement: Code MUST read a use case's identity, its grant, a permission's facts, and a role's permission set from the classes the analyzer package generates from the marks and the records, never from a hand-written copy.
provisions.rationale: Each of these facts is written once, on a record or in a mark. A hand-written table of them is a second source that drifts the first time a record changes. The generator writes them per project. `LiteSpecRegistry` answers a message type's use case (`UseCaseOf`), a marked type's use case (`UseCaseOfType`), a message type's grant (`GrantOf`), and in an API project an operation name's use case (`UseCaseOfOperation`). `LiteSpecPermissions` holds one constant and one entry per `permission/` record, and `LiteSpecRoles` holds each role's scope and the permissions its record allows. A role listing a permission missing from the records, and two records generating one name, stop at build time.
provisions.example: When the team adds a permission to Claimwick's `role/finance` record, `LiteSpecRoles.Of("role/finance").Permissions` carries it at the next build with no hand-written table to update, and `LiteSpecRegistry.GrantOf(typeof(ReimburseExpenseCommand))` answers the reimbursement grant.

provisions.heading: Identify an Aggregate Root by Its Mark and State Record
provisions.evidence: `litespec model check` reports `aggregate-unimplemented` (level S) for an aggregate record that no type with its mark and its state record, and no type deriving the aggregate root base, implements.
provisions.statement: The .NET stack reader MUST recognize a type that carries an `aggregate` mark and a `State` property backed by an abstract state record as an aggregate root.
provisions.rationale: A project claiming Implementation with its own layout and its own aggregate base keeps roots the LiteSpec base type does not describe. The aggregate mark names the record the type implements, and the state record states its lifecycle. Together they identify the root without the base type. A type with only the mark, or only the state record, does not state both facts, so it stays unrecognized. This provision states the `trace: yes` reading of the aggregate root beside the full contract the [domain page](domain.md) states.
provisions.example: The library loan type carries `/// <implements>aggregate/lending.loan</implements>` with a `LoanState State` property backed by the abstract `LoanState` record, so the reader treats it as the loan aggregate root and reads its public methods as aggregate methods.

provisions.heading: Read Every Declared Web and Worker Host
